{{nihongo|'''Hayasuihime Shrine'''|早吸日女神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Bungo Province]].

'''Hayasuihime Shrine''' (はやすいひめじんじゃ, はやすひめじんじゃ; also written '''Hayasuhime Shrine''') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Ōita (city)|Q199609|qid=Q199609}}, {{ill|Ōita Prefecture|Q133924|qid=Q133924}}. It is a {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932|lt=Engishiki-listed shrine}}, with former rank {{ill|Shakaku|ja|社格|ko|사격 (신토)|zh|社格|qid=Q10444029}} of prefectural shrine. Also called "Seki no Gongen-sama."

It enshrines {{ill|Magatsuhi-no-kami|Q11591203|qid=Q11591203|lt=Yasomagatsuhi-no-Kami}}, {{ill|Ōnaobi no Kami|ja|直毘神|zh|直毘神|qid=Q11581794|lt=Ōnaobi-no-Kami}}, the {{ill|Sumiyoshi sanjin|de|Sumiyoshi Sanjin|it|Sumiyoshi Sanjin|ja|住吉三神|mni|ꯁꯨꯃꯤꯌꯣꯁꯤ ꯁꯟꯖꯤꯟ|my|ဆုမိရောရှိနတ်သုံးပါး|pl|Sumiyoshi Sanjin|simple|Sumiyoshi sanjin|zh|住吉三神|qid=Q1114013}} (Sokotsutsu-no-kami, Nakatsutsu-no-kami, Uwatsutsu-no-kami), and various deities of earth and sea.

mẹjọ|zh|八腕目|zh_min_nan|Chiuⁿ-hî|zh_yue|八爪魚|qid=Q40152}}, calmed the tides, and offered it to him. He then made that sword the sacred object and enshrined the deity of purification gates (Hayasuihime), praying for national foundation.

Later, in {{ill|Taihō (era)|Q1346269|qid=Q1346269|lt=Taihō}} 1 (701), the shrine was moved to its current site. In {{ill|Keichō|Q1328185|qid=Q1328185}} 5 (1600), the shrine buildings were burned in war, but after becoming territory of {{ill|Kumamoto Domain|Q1194248|qid=Q1194248}}, they were rebuilt by {{ill|Katō Kiyomasa|Q1069843|qid=Q1069843}} in Keichō 7 (1602), and later rebuilt by successive lords of the {{ill|Hosokawa clan|Q2736120|qid=Q2736120}}. In March 2004, the honden, main gate, and shrine household building were designated {{ill|Tangible Cultural Property (Japan)|Q2901860|qid=Q2901860}} of Oita Prefecture.

The octopus that long guarded the sacred sword is treated as a shrine attendant spirit, and shrine priests never eat octopus. Even now, worshippers dedicate octopus drawings inscribed with wishes in a "tako-dachi" vow rite<ref>[https://www.i-manabi.jp/system/regionals/regionals/ecode:1/2/view/302 Uwa Sea and folk culture (FY1992), (1) East and west of Hayasui Strait (Sadamisaki and Sekizaki)] Lifelong Learning Information System, "Ehime no Kioku"</ref>.

A wisteria festival is held every year in early May<ref>[https://www.visit-oita.jp/events/detail/12393 Hayasuihime Shrine Wisteria Festival] Tourism Oita</ref>, and a grand summer festival is held in July, with floats and mikoshi parading through the town.

The haiden roof preserves a local tile technique and features unique roof tiles such as Urashima Tarō and a three-story pagoda.
